flags.title: Block-Granted Medicaid — Structural Underfunding Like PR
flags.summary: Like Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands receives Medicaid through a block grant with a fixed federal allocation. When the allocation runs out, the territory must fund 100% of additional costs. VI DHHS: 340-774-0930.

flags.title: Hovensa Refinery Closure (2012) — St. Croix Economic Collapse
flags.summary: The closure of the Hovensa oil refinery on St. Croix in 2012 devastated the island's economy. St. Croix lost its largest employer and tax base. Economic recovery is ongoing. Limetree Bay (partial reopening) has had environmental issues. St. Croix has distinct economic challenges from St. Thomas.

flags.title: Hurricanes Irma/Maria (2017) — Infrastructure Still Recovering
flags.summary: Hurricanes Irma and Maria (September 2017) caused catastrophic damage across all three islands. Infrastructure recovery continues, particularly on St. John and St. Croix. Verify current utility and housing status. FEMA: disasterassistance.gov. VI Housing Finance Authority: 340-777-4432.

flags.title: St. Croix vs St. Thomas — Distinct Service Landscapes
flags.summary: St. Croix and St. Thomas have distinct service landscapes. St. Thomas has more federal agency presence and healthcare infrastructure. St. Croix has higher poverty and fewer services. St. John has minimal services. Always verify which island the client is on before routing. Legal Services of the VI: 340-774-3016.

flags.title: No Federally Recognized Tribes — Taíno Not Recognized
flags.summary: The US Virgin Islands has no federally recognized tribes. The indigenous Taíno people are not federally recognized. Cultural preservation efforts exist but no IHS or tribal program eligibility.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: USVI Emergency Commitment
flags.message: VI involuntary psychiatric hold law: USVI Emergency Commitment. Statutory authority: 19 VIC § 582. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in VI retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in VI: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.
flags.statute: US Virgin Islands Involuntary Commitment Act

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: US Virgin Islands Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: US Virgin Islands Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
